title: Decision routing, scoring & explainability architecture notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the internal design for the policy evaluation component that sits between the control plane and the runtime router. It covers constraint normalization, scoring semantics, how evaluation results drive routing decisions, multi-region consistency considerations, and the explainability/telemetry output we persist for audits and debugging. This is an engineering working doc — includes proposals, tradeoffs, and operational runbook fragments.

Scope and intent:
- Not a user-facing policy language spec; focuses on the evaluation engine used by platform routing and guardrails.
- Covers both hard constraints (immediate reject/fallback) and soft constraints (score modifiers used for ranking route candidates).
- Emphasizes predictable, debuggable outputs (structured explain logs) that are cheap to sample/store but sufficient for root cause analysis.

High-level flow (simplified):
1) Control plane publishes policy bundle (versioned) -> pushed to region control agents.
2) Request arrives at edge router: attach request metadata + route context.
3) Router asks local evaluation engine for candidate scores and hard-gate decisions.
4) Evaluation engine applies constraint checks, computes per-candidate score, returns: {decision, score, explain_log_id}.
5) Router applies thresholds/fallback logic then selects final model/region and emits trace.

Evaluation engine responsibilities:
- Deterministically evaluate policy bundle against request context.
- Return compact explainability payload reference (not full verbose log by default).
- Apply region-local capacity and latency SLO constraints before soft scoring to avoid recommending overloaded targets.
- Support fast fast-path: precompiled constraint predicates for common checks.

Constraint semantics and normalization:
- Two classes: HARD (boolean gates) and SOFT (scoring modifiers).
- Constraint DSL (informal):
  - field comparator value (e.g. latency_ms < 120)
  - set membership (region in [us-west1, us-west2])
  - tier comparisons (customer_tier >= reserved)
  - model capabilities (capabilities contains "tool-calling")
- Normalization step: canonicalize field names, coerce units (ms vs s), expand shorthand (region aliases), and map deprecated keys to current ones. This prevents policy drift when bundles evolve.
- Evaluate HARD constraints first; any HARD failure yields decision=hard_reject with a short reason code.
- If HARD passes, evaluate SOFT constraints to produce a single composite score per candidate in range [0.0, 1.0].

Scoring internals (proposal):
- Base score: candidate is assigned a base_score (0.5 default) representing neutral preference.
- Each SOFT constraint has: type (boost/penalty), magnitude (linear or multiplicative), and decay window (how quickly effect fades).
- Composite computation (example):
  s = clamp(0.0, 1.0, base_score * product(1 + m_i) + sum(b_j))
  where m_i are multiplicative modifiers (e.g. -0.15 for 15% penalty) and b_j are additive boosts.
- Rationale: multiplicative modifiers represent relative cost/latency impacts; additive boosts represent categorical preference (e.g. favor same-region).
- Calibration: a daily job samples live traffic and metrics, uses ground-truth routing outcomes and SLOs to fit magnitude coefficients (offline).
- Bias controls: ensure no single signal can push score from >0.7 to <0.3 in one step; cap per-signal influence.

Explainability logs (design):
- Goal: concise, machine-readable traces that answer "why this candidate was chosen/rejected".
- Two-tiered approach:
  1) Summary record (always emitted, small): includes explain_log_id, request_id, timestamp, candidate_id, decision, final_score, top_3 contributing signals (names + short codes), policy_bundle_version, region_local_snapshot_id.
  2) Full trace (emitted only for sampled requests or on-demand): full evaluation tree, raw predicate values, intermediate numeric transforms, and link to runtime metrics (observed latency, queue depth).
- Storage: summary records -> high-throughput time-series store (Bigtable/Snowflake/S3 partitioned) for 90d retention. Full traces -> encrypted blob store (S3/GS) with 30d default retention and TTL tiers controlled by customer/enterprise contracts.
- PI/Privacy: mask any PII/payload elements before storing. Use deterministic hashing for identifiers when needed for joins.

Schema (summary record) example (stringified representation):
- explain_log_id: <uuid>
- request_id: <trace-id>
- timestamp: 2025-02-14T10:23:04Z
- candidate_id: model-x-quant8-usw2
- decision: allowed | fallback | hard_reject | degraded
- final_score: 0.63
- top_signals: ["latency_penalty:-0.12","region_match:+0.10","capacity_safety:-0.05"]
- policy_bundle_version: 2025-02-14T09:00Z
- region_snapshot: r-2025-02-14-usw2

Sampling policy and costs:
- Default sampling: 1% of requests for full traces, 100% for summary records.
- Dynamic sampling: increase sample rate on anomaly (score drift, error spike).
- Admin endpoints to fetch full traces on-demand for a request id (subject to retention/permission).

Multi-region consistency and control-plane interactions:
- Policy bundles are versioned atoms pushed to regional control agents. Strong ordering is important for rollouts: new bundle -> gradated push with canary region(s) -> global.
- Each region keeps a policy snapshot id and a local evaluation cache compiled from the bundle.
- For requests that route cross-region, we prefer deterministic scoring: include bundle snapshot id and policy-version in explain logs so post-hoc evaluation can replay behavior.
- Eventual consistency model: when bundles change, some regions may evaluate against older bundles for short windows. We handle this by adding a policy_freshness score penalty when snapshot_age > threshold to avoid routing to stale-policy regions unless explicitly pinned.

Control-plane API surfaces (sketch):
- PublishPolicy(bundle_id, bundle_payload, rollout_plan) -> returns rollout_id.
- QueryPolicyStatus(bundle_id) -> returns per-region status, snapshot ids.
- SnapshotCompile(bundle_id, target_region) -> precompile fast-path predicates and return compiled checksum for validation.
- ForceInvalidate(region, snapshot_id) -> evict local compiled cache (used in emergency rollbacks).

Runtime integrations and optimizations:
- Fast-path predicates compiled to bytecode/V8 for very common checks (region, tier, model tags) to keep evaluation <1ms for average candidate set.
- SIMD-friendly scoring math for vectorized scoring across many candidates simultaneously.
- Local capacity signals: exposed by region agent (current_gpu_free, avg_inflight, p99_latency_est) that are fed into constraint checks as ephemeral inputs.

Observability and alerting:
- Metrics to surface: per-bundle evaluation latency, fraction hard_rejects, score distribution percentiles, correlation of final_score to observed latency/cost.
- Dashboards: per-region heatmaps for score distribution and per-signal contribution.
- Alerts: sudden shift in score distribution (>3 sigma) for a bundle, or increase in fallback rate beyond threshold.

Operational playbook (short):
- Symptoms: increase in fallbacks to lower tier models.
  - Check policy bundle recent changes (rollout logs).
  - Inspect top_signals from explainability summaries for affected requests.
  - If bundle rollback needed: publish previous bundle and trigger ForceInvalidate for affected regions.
- Symptoms: scoring drift (final_score no longer predictive of latency).
  - Run calibration job against sampled traces.
  - Re-tune magnitudes and deploy as patch.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should the engine support user-defined functions in constraints? (danger: non-determinism + security) Proposal: allow a small sandboxed expression language, no arbitrary code.
- Full trace retention vs cost: propose tiered retention based on customer SLA and incident investigations.
- Offline replayability: ensure we capture enough context in summary to reconstruct evaluation without storing raw request payload. We need to standardize the request abstraction size/fields.

Immediate TODOs (near term):
- [ ] Formalize constraint DSL grammar and publish conformance tests. (owner: Julian)
- [ ] Implement summary schema proto and store adapters. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Build local snapshot invalidation API and test failover scenarios. (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Add dynamic sampling hook for anomaly detection pipeline. (owner: Ava)

Useful links and references:
- Confluence: decision-routing-v2 (design notes)
- Jira: JIRA-PLAT-1342 (policy bundle rollout automation)
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/route-eval-proto (proto for summary record)

Notes from discussion 2025-02-10:
- Teams prefer small, deterministic summary records by default; full traces only during incidents.
- Capacity signals must be strongly bounded and time-windowed; remember load spikes can make signals stale very quickly.

Appendix (example constraint cases):
- HARD: (region in [eu-central1]) AND (customer_tier == reserved) -> enforce dedicated-only models.
- SOFT: if p99_estimated_latency_ms > 120 then apply multiplicative penalty -0.25 to candidate score.
- SOFT: same_region_bonus: if candidate_region == request_region then additive +0.10.

End of note.
